learning_outcomes.text_as_printed: Understand the physical diversity of India  Identify and explain the major physical divisions of India:
Northern Mountains (Himalayas)
Northern Horizontal Areas
Southern Plateau
Coastal Horizontal Areas
Desert (Thar Desert)
Islands (Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep)  These features will be identified on the physical map of India.
Himalayan Mountains
Describe the features of the Himalayan range (snow-capped peaks, valleys, glaciers).
They will understand the importance of the Himalayas (the origin of rivers, stopping the cold air and bringing rain).
Mount Everest, Kanchenjunga, and K2 peaks are identified.
Northern Horizontal Areas
The northern plains are known as the food repositories of India.
Name the major rivers (Ganga, Yamuna, Brahmaputra) and their importance in agriculture.
He explains how these horizontal areas influenced the Harappan, Mauryan and Mughal empires.
Southern Plateau
He distinguishes between the Malwa plateau and the southern plateau (Deccan).
The major mountain ranges are named (Aravalli, Vindhya, Satpura, Western and Eastern Ghats).
They will understand the mineral wealth and historical significance of the Chalukya, Vijayanagara Empire.
Coastal horizontal areas and islands
He distinguishes between the western coastal plain (Konkan, Malabar) and the east coast plane (Coramandala, Sarkar).
The major ports are named (Mumbai, Chennai, Mangalore, Kochi).
Identify the lifestyle, food habits and occupations (fishing, coconut crop) of the coastal people.
Thar Desert
Describing the features of the Thar Desert (hot weather, sandy hills, osis).
Explain how people and animals (camels) adjust in the desert.
Jaipur, Jaisalmer, and Mount Abu are known as important desert cities.
Rivers of India
Rivers are classified into North India (Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra) and South India (Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery, Narmada, Tapi).
Understand the difference between perennial (Himalayan) and seasonal (southern) rivers.
They will discuss pollution and conservation efforts of Ganga-Yamuna rivers.
Weather and Seasons  The four seasons of India are identified:
Winter (December-February)
Summer (March-May)
Southwest Monsoon (June-September)
Retreating monsoon (October-November)  Explain how monsoon winds affect agriculture.  Identify areas prone to heavy rainfall (Mausinram, Western Ghats) and drought.
Biodiversity and Conservation
Naming different types of forests (Parnapati, Sadabahara, Mangrove).
Identify protected wildlife sanctuaries (Gir, Kaziranga, Sundarbans).
List endangered animals (tiger, elephant, rhinoceros).
Understand the effects of deforestation and the need for conservation.
Human-Environment Relationship
Explain how physical features influence culture, food, clothing and architecture (e.g. sloping roofs in coastal areas, sangam tree buildings in Rajasthan).
They will discuss environmental challenges (river pollution, deforestation, climate change).
Suggest ways to protect natural resources (purification of rivers), Tree planting, wildlife conservation).
